source.name: ASTRA Bio wave 1 — Plant Kingdom
source.license: Original syllabus-based practice questions (exam-frequent themes; not verbatim past papers)

questions.stem: The plant body of algae is typically a
questions.explanation: Algae lack true roots, stems and leaves; the body is a simple thallus.

questions.stem: Green algae store food mainly as
questions.explanation: Chlorophyceae have chlorophyll a and b and store starch, like higher plants.

questions.stem: The brown pigment characteristic of Phaeophyceae is
questions.explanation: Fucoxanthin masks chlorophyll and gives brown algae their colour.

questions.stem: Agar used in microbiology is obtained mainly from
questions.explanation: Red algae Gelidium and Gracilaria yield agar.

questions.stem: Bryophytes are called amphibians of the plant kingdom because they
options: need water for fertilisation though they live on land
possess xylem vessels in all genera
questions.explanation: They occupy moist land but motile sperms still require a film of water.

questions.stem: The first land plants to possess vascular tissues (xylem and phloem) are the
questions.explanation: Pteridophytes are vascular cryptogams; bryophytes lack true vascular tissue.

questions.stem: In gymnosperms the ovules remain
options: inside an ovary that becomes a fruit
questions.explanation: Gymnosperm means naked seed: ovules are not enclosed in an ovary.

questions.stem: Double fertilisation is a unique feature of
questions.explanation: One male gamete fuses with the egg and the other with polar nuclei only in flowering plants.

questions.stem: A haplontic life cycle, with a dominant haploid plant body, is seen in
questions.explanation: Many green algae (e.g. Spirogyra) are haplontic; seed plants are diplontic.

questions.stem: Sphagnum is economically important because it
options: is the source of all cereals
questions.explanation: Peat moss absorbs water and its deposits form peat used as fuel and in horticulture.

questions.stem: Volvox, Ulothrix and Chara are members of
questions.explanation: These are textbook green algae (Chlorophyceae).

questions.stem: Heterospory, regarded as a precursor of the seed habit, occurs in
questions.explanation: Selaginella, Salvinia and Marsilea produce micro- and megaspores; this foreshadows seeds.

questions.stem: Coralloid roots associated with nitrogen-fixing cyanobacteria are a feature of
questions.explanation: Cycas coralloid roots harbour Anabaena/Nostoc; Pinus roots are typically mycorrhizal.

questions.stem: Which statement about algae is incorrect?
options: The plant body is usually a thallus
They possess chlorophyll and are photosynthetic
They always produce seeds inside fruits
questions.explanation: Algae are thalloid phototrophs; seeds and fruits appear only in spermatophytes.

questions.stem: Chlorophyceae are characterised by chlorophylls
questions.explanation: Green algae share chlorophyll a and b with land plants; brown algae have a and c.

questions.stem: Stored food in brown algae is chiefly
questions.explanation: Phaeophyceae accumulate laminarin and mannitol; red algae store floridean starch.

questions.stem: Which pigment is typical of Rhodophyceae?
options: chlorophyll b as the only chlorophyll
questions.explanation: Red algae have chlorophyll a (and d) plus phycoerythrin, which masks other pigments.

questions.stem: In bryophytes the dominant, independent generation is the
questions.explanation: The green leafy or thalloid plant is haploid; the sporophyte is attached and dependent.

questions.stem: The independent photosynthetic prothallus of a fern is
questions.explanation: Pteridophyte spores grow into a small haploid prothallus that bears sex organs.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a gymnosperm?
questions.explanation: Pinus, Cycas, Cedrus and Ginkgo are gymnosperms; the others are a liverwort, a green alga and a fern.

questions.stem: Which statement about angiosperms is incorrect?
options: Ovules are enclosed in an ovary
Seeds are enclosed in a fruit
Double fertilisation produces a zygote and endosperm
Ovules are always exposed on woody cones
questions.explanation: Exposed ovules on cones characterise gymnosperms, not flowering plants.

questions.stem: A diplontic life cycle is the rule in
questions.explanation: Seed plants have a dominant diploid sporophyte; bryophytes are haplo-diplontic with a dominant gametophyte.

questions.stem: Algin is a hydrocolloid obtained from
questions.explanation: Alginates come from phaeophycean walls (Laminaria, Sargassum, Macrocystis).

questions.stem: Which alga is incorrectly placed in Chlorophyceae?
questions.explanation: Laminaria is a kelp (Phaeophyceae); the others are green algae.

questions.stem: Which pair of life-cycle type and example is incorrect?
questions.explanation: Pinus is diplontic. Fucus/Sargassum are diplontic brown algae; mosses are haplo-diplontic.

questions.stem: Identify the incorrect match.
questions.explanation: Marchantia is a liverwort without true vascular tissue; the other matches are standard.
